chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from one of our companions, from al-Ash'ath ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Hafsh ibn Kharjah, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: A man asked him about the statement of the Murji'ah regarding disbelief and faith, and he said: Indeed, they argue against us and say, 'Just as the disbeliever among us is the disbeliever with Allah, so too we find that the believer, when he acknowledges his faith, is the believer with Allah.'

So he (peace be upon him) said: Glory be to Allah! And how can these two be equal? Disbelief is an acknowledgment by the servant, so he is not required after his acknowledgment to provide proof. But faith is a claim that is not valid except with proof, and its proof is his deed and his intention. So when they agree, the servant is a believer with Allah.

And disbelief is present in any one of these three aspects: from intention, or speech, or deed. And the rulings flow upon the speech and the deed. So how many are there whom the believers testify to having faith, and the rulings of the believers flow upon him, yet he is a disbeliever with Allah? And the one who applies the rulings of the believers upon him is correct, based on the apparent of his speech and his deed.

key_terms.الْمُرْجِئَة: The Murji'ah, a theological sect that deferred judgment on sinners and emphasized verbal declaration of faith.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between faith in the eyes of people and faith in the eyes of Allah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refutes the Murji'ah sect's reduction of faith to mere verbal declaration, establishing that true Iman requires the convergence of intention (niyyah) and action (amal). This hadith underscores the Shia doctrine of 'Tawassu' al-Iman' (the spreading of faith to the limbs), distinguishing between apparent judgment (hukm zahiri) in this world and ultimate reality (haqiqah) with Allah, where a person may be deemed a believer socially yet be a disbeliever divinely if their inner conviction is absent.
